s1.quote: Carib Cargo , a popular dive site, is an old interisland trader that sits upright in about 70 feet of water.

s2.quote: It lays upright at 65 feet (19.8m) in sand surrounded by seagrass. Over time the wreck has started to crumble and penetration is not advised.

highlights.text: Stingrays, turtles and reef sharks around the wreck

hazards.text: Wreck is crumbling; penetration not advised

summary.text: An upright inter-island cargo ship on sand at the edge of the Man of War Shoal Marine Park off Great Bay, in roughly 65-70 ft. Rays, turtles and reef sharks visit; the hull is deteriorating, so stay outside.

s1.quote: HMS Proselyte , a stunning wreck that was once a 32-gun Royal Navy frigate. … this stunning vessel came to rest on her starboard side about 50 feet down.

s2.quote: Today the wreck is scatter and sits on its starboard side in 20 to 55 feet of water. … Depending on the sea conditions this site may be subject to surges.

highlights.text: Cannons, anchors and ballast bars under coral growth

summary.text: The scattered remains of a 1801 Royal Navy frigate on the Man of War Shoal just off Philipsburg. Cannons, anchors and ballast bars lie under heavy coral in about 20-55 ft; surge can be felt.

s1.quote: The Fish Bowl gets its name from the variety of fish that are found on the reef. … The depth ranges from 40 feet to 60 feet. There is a large arch that you can swim through

s2.quote: Just off Great Bay , we have several options, including Carib Cargo, Teigland, Fish Bowl, and Mike’s Maze.

highlights.text: Swim-through arch with barracuda; reef sharks

hazards.text: Can become dangerous in rough seas

summary.text: A fish-rich reef in 40-60 ft near the harbour entrance off Great Bay, reached by boat. A swim-through arch often holds barracuda and reef sharks are common; suitable for all levels but rough seas make it hazardous.
